The updated prototype checks out (auto-fill, save, and duplicate detection all working, no errors). The review version is live at **http://maker:4001**.

I've folded in four of your requests. Please try them one at a time so I can catch your reaction to each.

**1 — Saving with the icon and preview**
Paste this and press **Save**:
```
https://www.smashingmagazine.com/calm-interfaces
```
Notice the panel now shows a **site icon** and a **preview image** it collected from the page, alongside the title and description. Then press **Save to my list** and see how the icon and preview appear on the card.
> *Two things I decided here, please judge them:* I show the preview as a thumbnail on the left of each card; and when a page has no preview image, I show a small "no preview" placeholder instead of leaving a gap. (In this prototype the icon/preview are stand-ins — the real app would pull the actual ones from the page.)

**2 — The "Read later" marking**
In that same panel you'll have seen a **Read later** switch. I set it to **on by default**, on the assumption that most things you save are things you still intend to read. Save one link with it on and one with it off, and check the difference on the cards (a small "Read later" tag). Tell me whether *on-by-default* matches how you'd actually use it, or whether you'd rather decide each time.

**3 — Label suggestions**
Save another link — try `https://developer.mozilla.org/reduce` — and in the **Labels** field, start with the ones you've used before appearing as clickable chips beneath it. Click one to reuse it. Check whether that keeps you consistent the way you hoped.

**4 — Pasting a link you already saved**
Paste the Smashing Magazine link again. Instead of making a second copy, it should recognize it and open **your existing saved one** so you can update it. See whether that behaviour feels right.
> *One decision to judge:* I chose to quietly take you into editing the existing bookmark (rather than, say, warning you "this is a duplicate"). Is that the right instinct?

---

One request I've **not** built yet, on purpose: **opening the original page** when you select a title or card. There's more than one sensible way to do that (for instance, the whole card opening the page vs. just the title, and where the page opens), so rather than guess, I'd like to show you a couple of side-by-side options to compare next — once you've reacted to the four above.
